title: Building Healthier Screen Habits
hook: You don't need to quit your phone — just out-design it. A few small tweaks beat willpower for taking back your attention.
key_points: Keep screens out of the bedroom and stop scrolling before bed to protect sleep.
Turn off non-essential notifications so your phone stops interrupting you.
Use screens with intention — open an app for a reason, not by reflex.
Take movement and screen breaks; look away regularly to rest your eyes and mind.
content_html: The hard part about cutting back on screens is that the devices are designed to be hard to put down. The NHS's advice sidesteps the willpower battle: change your environment and defaults so the healthier choice is the easy one.
extra_html: The NHS suggests a handful of practical tactics for using technology more mindfully. Keep screens out of the bedroom and stop scrolling before bed, so light and stimulation don't eat into your sleep. Switch off notifications you don't truly need, which removes the constant tug that fragments attention. Use devices with intention — open an app to do a specific thing, then close it, rather than reaching for your phone by reflex when you're bored or anxious. And build in breaks: stand up, move, and look away from the screen regularly to rest your eyes and reset your focus. None of these require an all-or-nothing digital detox; they're small adjustments that, stacked together, hand you back a surprising amount of attention and calm.

related.title: Screens and Your Wellbeing
related.hook: It's not just how many hours you're on a screen — it's how and when. The same phone can leave you rested or wrecked depending on use.

related.title: Building Better Sleep Habits
related.hook: Good sleep is mostly built in the hours before bed. A handful of simple habits — collectively called sleep hygiene — do more than any gadget.

related.title: Quick Ways to Calm Down
related.hook: When stress spikes, you can't think your way calm — but you can breathe your way there. A few simple tools work in minutes, anywhere.

related.title: Your Brain Wasn't Built for This Much Bad News
related.hook: We're wired to watch for danger — useful when threats were local. A nonstop feed of global bad news hijacks that instinct, and the fix isn't tuning out but changing how you tune in.

flashcards.prompt: Which habit most directly protects your sleep from screens?

choices.text: Keeping screens out of the bedroom and stopping scrolling before bed
Switching your phone to a darker wallpaper
Replying to messages faster so you finish sooner

flashcards.explanation_html: The NHS suggests keeping devices out of the bedroom and avoiding screens before bed, since late use can interfere with winding down and sleep.

flashcards.prompt: Name two practical ways to make screen time more intentional.
flashcards.back_html:
• Turn off non-essential notifications so the phone stops interrupting you.
  • Open an app for a specific reason rather than out of reflex, and take regular breaks to move and rest your eyes.
